items.title: ‘Completely avoidable’: Review ordered after Edmonton man dies waiting in ER
items.description: The Alberta government has ordered a review after a 44-year-old man died of an apparent cardiac arrest while waiting for care in an Edmonton emergency department.

items.title: Wintry weather warnings issued for parts of Nova Scotia, New Brunswick
items.description: Environment Canada has issued  yellow warnings  for wintry conditions in parts of Nova Scotia and New Brunswick.

items.title: Man charged with 2nd-degree murder in northern Alberta shooting deaths
items.description: A man has been charged with two counts of second-degree murder after two people were killed near Grande Prairie, Alta. early Saturday morning.

items.title: New items eligible for Ontario blue bins, but will they actually get recycled?
items.description: Ontarians will be able to put more products into the blue bin in 2026 as the province moves toward a privately operated recycling program. But some are worried more sorting doesn't mean there's a real market to recycle the products into something else.

items.title: Bird never seen before in Canada draws crowds to Vancouver park
items.description: The taiga flycatcher has never before been seen in Canada. At least, not until this holiday season when a bird watcher spotted the rare avian specimen in a Vancouver park.

items.title: Birders flock to Vancouver beach to see rare bird native to Russia
items.description: Dozens of birders descended on Vancouver’s Sunset Beach Park on Sunday to catch a rare glimpse of a bird that avian enthusiasts say has never been recorded in Canada before.

items.title: Canadian food banks record over 4 million visits this year
items.description: The Daily Bread Food Bank in Toronto is seeing a spike in young adults, between the ages of 19 and 44, in need of a food bank. The CBC speaks with the food bank’s CEO, Neil Hetherington.

CN Rail says no threat to safety after train derails in Winnipeg
items.description: A CN Rail train derailed on Sunday in Winnipeg's South Osborne area, with eight cars tipping over and a ninth remaining upright. Officials say there is no threat to public safety.

items.title: Before robbing trains in the States, the Sundance Kid was a cowboy in Alberta
items.description: Harry Longabaugh — better known as the Sundance Kid — is perhaps most famous for his daring bank and train robberies as part of Butch Cassidy’s Wild Bunch. But the American outlaw’s short stint as a cowboy and businessman in southern Alberta is a lesser-known chapter of Wild West history.
